message.text:
q19.

Connect RPC (used by the browser client, mounted at `/memos.api.v1.*`) — `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go`, with the per-RPC wrappers in `server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go`; wired up in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (lines 139–144)

REST via gRPC-Gateway (mounted at `/api/v1/*`) — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (line 108, `RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer`), using the generated gateway code `proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.gw.go`

Both protocols are registered in `RegisterGateway` in `v1.go` and both dispatch into the same `APIV1Service` methods, so there's one copy of the business logic. The REST side registers via `RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer` on a `runtime.NewServeMux` with a gateway auth middleware, and the resulting handler is attached to Echo:

```126:129:server/router/api/v1/v1.go
	handler := echo.WrapHandler(http.MaxBytesHandler(gwMux, maxAPIRequestBytes))

	gwGroup.Any("/api/v1/*", handler)
	gwGroup.Any("/file/*", handler)
```

The Connect side builds a separate `http.ServeMux` and calls `RegisterConnectHandlers`, which registers `apiv1connect.NewMemoServiceHandler(s, opts...)` alongside the other seven services (`connect_handler.go:40`). Its interceptor chain — metadata, logging, recovery, and auth — is configured at `v1.go:133`. The `ConnectServiceHandler` type embeds `*APIV1Service` and each method (for example `CreateMemo` at `connect_services.go:307`) just unwraps `connect.Request` and delegates.

Note that the gateway registration uses the `...HandlerServer` variants, which call the service in-process rather than dialing a gRPC port, so there is no separately listening native gRPC server here.
